market_commentary.overview:
Sale & Purchase: The second-hand market kept up its pace, with a further thirty vessels reported sold 
across all sectors (15 bulkers, 11 tankers, 2 containerships, 1 gas carrier and 1 multi-purpose vessel). 
Dry bulk accounted for half of the week's business, with Handysizes once again the most traded size and 
older Capesizes and Panamaxes finding buyers at firm levels. Tanker activity, by contrast, slowed from last 
week's pace as buyers and sellers took stock of the correction in freight rates, although the deals concluded 
show no sign of values giving ground. 
In the bulker sector, 15 vessels changed hands: 2 Capesizes, 1 Post-Panamax, 1 Panamax, 1 Ultramax, 3 
Supramaxes and 7 Handysizes. Korean buyers H-Line Shipping paid USD 39.7 mill for the Chinese-built 
Capesize EVER ABILITY (180,133 dwt, 2011 Qingdao Beihai/China), with her special survey freshly passed. 
The price level is in line with the USD 40 mill paid by Norwegian buyers in early October for the same-age 
GOLDEN MYRTALIA (177,979 dwt, 2011 SWS/China). This suggests that appetite for older Capesizes is 
healthier than it appeared a week ago.
In the Post-Panamax segment, the Japanese-built AURIGA OCEAN (93,549 dwt, 2008 Namura/Japan) was 
sold for USD 15 mill, a strong price for her age as it matches the level paid last week for the two-year-
younger, Chinese-built SHUN CHANG (93,322 dwt, 2010 Yangfan/China). 
In the Kamsarmax segment, the 2019 Oshima-built TAHO AUSTRALIA (81,788 dwt), which we reported last 
week as rumoured at region USD 38 mill, is now understood to have been concluded at USD 38 - 39 mill, 
level with the USD 38.5 mill achieved in early October by the same-age BABITONGA (81,770 dwt, 2019 
Tsuneishi/Japan). 
Vintage Panamaxes with favourable survey positions also attracted buyers: the ANASTASIA (75,331 dwt, 
2006 STX/Korea, SS due 01/2031) fetched region USD 13.2 - 14 mill, in line with the USD 13.6 - 13.8 mill 
paid at the end of October for the Japanese-built AMOY SUNNY (76,598 dwt, 2006 Imabari/Japan), 
although we understand from a trusted source that the ANASTASIA deal is an older sale that has only now 
come to light. 
In the geared sizes, the Crown 63-type Ultramax CARAVOS LIBERTY (63,301 dwt, 2013 Yangzhou 
Dayang/China, SS/DD due 02/2028) was committed at USD 24.5 mill, a strong level for a Chinese-built unit 
when set against the region USD 24 mill reported last week for the same-age, Japanese-built DIAMOND

October for the BULK GUATEMALA (61,446 dwt, 2013 Iwagi/Japan). 
Clients of ADNOC, who were behind three tanker purchases last week, also turned to the dry side, paying 
USD 20 mill for the Supramax BAO SHENG (58,110 dwt, 2011 Tsuneishi Zhoushan/China), a premium of 
some USD 4.5 mill over the excess USD 15.5 mill reported last week for the same-age TONY SMITH (56,498 
dwt, 2011 Qingshan/China). The one-year-younger AFRICA NOVA (56,781 dwt, 2012 Ningbo Beilun 
Lantian/China, SS/DD due 06/2027) was sold for USD 13.8 mill, below the level reported for the older TONY 
SMITH.
The Handysize segment was again the busiest. Turkish buyers paid region USD 21.5 - 22 mill for the 2016 
Namura-built AFRICAN OWL (34,382 dwt, SS due 01/2031), just above the USD 20 - 21 mill offers we 
reported last week. In the larger Handysizes, the Japanese-built DARYA KAVRI (37,981 dwt, 2017 I-S 
Shipyard/Japan, SS due 02/2027, DD due 03/2027) is rumoured to have seen offers in excess of USD 24 mill; 
offers were invited on 13 November basis charter-free delivery 1 February - 15 March 2027, with her 
surveys due. The AM PRINCESS (31,963 dwt, 2013 Guangzhou Wenchong/China) achieved high USD 13 mill, 
about USD 1 mill more than the USD 12.5 mill paid last month for her one-year-younger sister AM 
PRESTIGE (31,956 dwt, 2014) and above the USD 13 mill reported at the end of October for the same-age 
BAO SHINE (32,203 dwt, 2013 Jiangmen Nanyang/China), a clear sign of how quickly values in this size are 
moving. 
Among older Japanese units, the UBC SANTOS (31,568 dwt, 2008 Saiki/Japan) is reported at USD 11.5 mill, 
although the deal may have been concluded some time ago; for comparison, the two-year-younger, 
Hakodate-built sisters PAIWAN WISDOM and DAIWAN WISDOM (31,967 dwt & 31,833 dwt, 2010 
Hakodate/Japan) fetched USD 11.75 mill each in late October. 
The SUNNY HONOR (32,040 dwt, 2004 Hakodate/Japan) is reported at USD 7 mill, below the USD 8.5 mill 
achieved in September by the one-year-older FIRST BROTHER (32,385 dwt, 2003 Kanda/Japan), while the 
vintage ABK TIGER (28,473 dwt, 2002 Imabari/Japan) and DUYEN HAI 1 (28,456 dwt, 2001 Kanda/Japan) 
fetched USD 5.3 mill and USD 5.5 mill respectively. The same-vintage EAST WIND I (28,458 dwt, 2002 
Japan, logs fitted) achieved a slightly firmer USD 5.85 mill. The Indian-built MALLIKA NAREE (30,195 dwt, 
2008 Hindustan/India), reported earlier this week as sold for USD 7.85 mill gross (USD 7.65 mill net), is 
understood to be back on the market after the sale failed, as her buyers did not perform.
On the tanker front, 11 sales were reported. The LR1 sisters CLEAROCEAN FUKU and CLEAROCEAN FUYO 
(73,720 dwt & 73,666 dwt, 2008 New Times/China) were sold en bloc for USD 80 mill, or USD 40 mill each, 
effectively matching the USD 39.5 mill reported two weeks ago for the three-year-younger, Japanese-built 
KAMOME VICTORIA (74,908 dwt, 2011 Minaminippon/Japan). From the same yard, the one-year-younger 
CONSTANTINOS (73,307 dwt, 2009 New Times/China) also fetched USD 40 mill.
In the MR segment, the PYXIS KARTERIA (46,652 dwt, 2013 Hyundai Mipo/Korea) was agreed at USD 37 
mill, almost double the USD 20 mill her sellers paid in 2021 and a step up from the USD 35 mill and USD 36 
mill paid in recent weeks for the same-age PACIFIC ONYX (49,996 dwt, 2013 Onomichi/Japan) and 
ARDMORE ENDEAVOUR (49,859 dwt, 2013 STX/Korea), while the older GRAND ACE6 (46,192 dwt, 2007 
STX/Korea, SS due 02/2027) fetched USD 20.5 mill, in line with the USD 20 - 20.2 mill paid recently for the 
same-age HANSA OSLO and LS NEPTUNE. 
Japanese tonnage also attracted Greek interest, with the KOBE and TOKYO (46,622 dwt & 44,999 dwt, 2009 
Naikai/Japan) sold en bloc to Greek buyers for USD 27.5 mill each.

In the larger sizes, clients of Volare acquired two VLCCs in internal transactions at USD 210 mill each: the 
newly delivered VENI VIDI VICI (308,285 dwt, 2026 Dalian/China) and the ten-year-old, scrubber-fitted 
BANGLADESH PROSPERITY (308,285 dwt, 2016 China, SS/DD passed 09/2026), which her sellers had 
bought in October 2025 for USD 85 mill as the LANDBRIDGE PROSPERITY. The coiled JASMINE KNUTSEN 
(148,706 dwt, 2005 Korea) is also reported sold at an undisclosed price, while at the smaller end Indonesian 
buyers paid USD 37.25 mill for the modern, epoxy-coated BAGSHOT (17,933 dwt, 2023 Hyundai 
Mipo/Korea).
For a detailed review and additional information regarding this week's transactions, kindly refer to our

market_commentary.demolition:
The number of reported recycling deals picked up, but the market remains short of 
conventional candidates: most of the business involved small units, damaged vessels and specialised 
tonnage, and prices were rarely disclosed. The largest unit was the 1977-built FPSO GIMBOA (33,700 ldt), 
sold on 'as is' Walvis Bay basis with delivery to the Indian subcontinent in buyers' option, while the 1972-
built mining vessel GRAND BANKS (6,369 ldt) fetched USD 610 - 612 per LT at auction 'as is' South Africa, a 
level that reflects her specification rather than the general market. Turkey took the MR tanker MINERVA 
VIRGO (11,110 ldt, 2006) together with the drone-damaged GOLDEN SAPLING and AROYAT, while the 
general cargo CHANG FENG HAI (2,343 ldt, 2006) was sold for recycling in China.
Price indications were more or less steady. Bangladesh softened but remains the best-paying destination. 
India recorded the largest gains, as recyclers returned from the Diwali holidays. Pakistan stayed quiet, with 
recyclers stepping back until prices soften. Turkey softened on reduced demand following an accident at 
one of the country's major steel mills.
